title: My neighbour asked me to stop pacing 🚪

hook_text: At 2:50 in the morning my neighbour knocked on the wall and asked me to stop pacing.

scenes.narration: At 2:50 in the morning my neighbour knocked on the wall and asked me to stop pacing.
I was lying in bed. I had not moved in an hour. I live in a block of flats, and the wall between us is so thin I can hear him turn the pages of his paper.
I called through the wall and said it was not me. He knocked again, three taps, and said, then who is walking round your flat in your slippers?
I listened. At first there was nothing. Then I heard it. Slow steps in the hallway, the soft flap of a heel against a slipper, exactly the way I walk.
The steps stopped outside my bedroom. The door handle dipped by a few millimetres, and rose again. Like somebody testing whether it was locked.
My neighbour knocked a fourth time, quietly this time. He whispered, I have been listening to you walk every night for a month, and some nights there are two of you.
I asked which night was the first. He took a long time to answer. He said, the night you came home and told me you had lost your keys.
I have never lost my keys. And I have never spoken to the man next door. The handle dipped once more, and a voice outside my door said, in my voice, please let me in.
So tell me. Do you open the door, or knock back on the wall?
